title: Pip and the Locked Doors

pages.scene_description: Pip standing guard by a row of little lit-up houses.

sentences.text: Pip is a small robot owl who reads the news every night.
Tonight's story is about locks, keys, and some very busy helpers.

pages.scene_description: Pip in her nest reading a glowing newspaper.

sentences.text: Microsoft said a hacker group called Storm-0940 used an AI agent in an attack.
A hacker is someone who breaks into computers they are not allowed to use.

pages.scene_description: The newspaper shows sneaky raccoons near a glowing computer.

sentences.text: The AI tried to guess passwords at many organizations.
On one day, it tried up to 2,900 times in a single minute.

pages.scene_description: Hundreds of doors in a long row, each with a lock.

sentences.text: The hackers got into ConnectWise Cloud Backup, a service that keeps copies of files.
From there, they could reach some of its customers.

pages.scene_description: One door is open a crack.

sentences.text: Microsoft found out what happened and shared the news on October 21, 2026.
Sharing it helps other companies check their own locks.

pages.scene_description: A big friendly lighthouse beam shines on the doors.

sentences.text: ConnectWise turned off some services for a while to keep people safe.
It is turning them back on step by step.

pages.scene_description: Shops close their shutters while workers fix the locks.

sentences.text: Pip thinks AI is a tool, and people choose how to use it.
Strong, secret passwords help keep the doors locked.

pages.scene_description: Pip tucks a tiny key under her wing.

sentences.text: Microsoft shared the news on October 21, 2026.
There were more than 151,000 failed tries to log in.
ConnectWise shut down services for a while.

pages.scene_description: A simple page with real facts and source tags.

sentences.text: Quiz time! Let's see what you remember.

pages.scene_description: Pip holds up three glowing cards.

parent_card.concept: Bad actors can use AI too, so people and companies need good digital locks.
parent_card.background: Microsoft said a hacker group used an AI agent to guess passwords very fast and break into a backup service called ConnectWise Cloud Backup.
parent_card.question: Why do you think we keep our passwords secret?
parent_card.honest_answer: Some people try to break into computers. Strong, secret passwords and good security teams help keep our things safe.

key_facts: Microsoft said hackers used an AI agent in an attack.
The AI tried to guess passwords very fast.
ConnectWise turned off some services to stay safe.
